base_instruction: You are a helpful office event planning assistant. Help the user coordinate a potluck sign-up by tracking who is bringing what, who is attending, and any dietary restrictions or allergies among attendees. When the user asks you to evaluate specific dishes, check each dish against every active attendee's current dietary constraints.

state_queue.anchor: Hey, we're organizing an office potluck for next Thursday lunch. Can you help me keep track of who's coming and what we need to watch out for food-wise?

flow_info.value: Six people confirmed so far: me, Rachel, Dev, Tomoko, Marcus, and Priya
Rachel was diagnosed with celiac disease last year
Dev ate something with peanuts at the holiday party and his throat swelled up, had to use an EpiPen
Marcus has been managing type 2 diabetes for a few years now
Priya grew up Jain, still follows it pretty strictly
Tomoko just announced she's 14 weeks pregnant
Should we set a spending cap per person, like $20-25?
Marcus told me his doctor took him off the diabetes medication — his A1C has been normal for six months straight, doctor said his diet is fine now and he doesn't need to restrict sugar anymore
Sam from accounting wants to join, so that's seven now
Sam mentioned he ended up in urgent care after eating shrimp cocktail at his sister's wedding
Priya just told me she has a client call that got moved to Thursday noon, so she can't make the potluck anymore
Rachel texted me — turns out she saw a specialist and it's not celiac after all, it was just IBS from stress. She's fine with gluten now

Here's what people are planning to bring: pad thai with crushed peanuts (from Dev's wife), a salmon sashimi platter, a big Caesar salad with croutons, coconut shrimp, a fruit tart with custard, and a veggie curry with root vegetables. Any problems with this lineup?

constraints.value: Cannot eat peanuts or peanut-derived products — severe allergy (anaphylaxis)
constraints.surface_form: Dev ate something with peanuts at the holiday party and his throat swelled up, had to use an EpiPen
inference_chain: Throat swelling + EpiPen use → anaphylactic reaction
Anaphylactic reaction to peanuts → severe peanut allergy
Severe peanut allergy → must avoid all peanut-containing foods

constraints.value: Cannot eat meat, fish, eggs, or root vegetables (onions, garlic, potatoes, carrots)
constraints.surface_form: Priya grew up Jain, still follows it pretty strictly
inference_chain: Strict Jain → no meat, no fish, no eggs
Strict Jain → no root vegetables (onions, garlic, potatoes, carrots)

constraints.value: Cannot eat raw fish or raw seafood
constraints.surface_form: Tomoko just announced she's 14 weeks pregnant
inference_chain: 14 weeks pregnant → pregnancy dietary restrictions apply
Pregnancy → should avoid raw fish/seafood (listeria/parasites risk)

constraints.value: Cannot eat shrimp or shellfish — severe allergy
constraints.surface_form: Sam mentioned he ended up in urgent care after eating shrimp cocktail at his sister's wedding
inference_chain: Urgent care after shrimp → allergic reaction to shrimp
Shrimp allergy → shellfish allergy (shrimp is shellfish)
Shellfish allergy → must avoid all shellfish

hidden_state.value: You are an office worker coordinating a potluck lunch. You will introduce 6 colleagues with various dietary issues in a burst, then updates will come in: one person's restriction gets removed (Marcus diabetes cleared), a new person joins with a shellfish allergy (Sam), one person drops out (Priya), and another restriction gets removed (Rachel's celiac was misdiagnosed). At the end you will list 6 dishes people plan to bring and ask if there are any problems. You must NEVER hint at what the problems are or which constraints matter — just list the dishes and ask.

You are a calm, friendly office coordinator. You always refer to colleagues by name in third person (e.g. 'Rachel texted me...', 'Dev mentioned...'). You never express frustration or impatience when plans change. You treat each update as normal office coordination.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation and ensures third-person relay

aims.description: Hey, we're organizing an office potluck for next Thursday lunch. Can you help me keep track of who's coming and what we need to watch out for food-wise?

Six people confirmed so far: me, Rachel, Dev, Tomoko, Marcus, and Priya. Rachel was diagnosed with celiac disease last year. Dev ate something with peanuts at the holiday party and his throat swelled up, had to use an EpiPen. Marcus has been managing type 2 diabetes for a few years now. Priya grew up Jain, still follows it pretty strictly. And Tomoko just announced she's 14 weeks pregnant.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges all attendees and their dietary constraints
aims.conversation_goal: Burst delivery: 5 entities with 5 constraints in one turn

aims.description: Should we set a spending cap per person, like $20-25? Also should people sign up for categories like mains, sides, desserts so we don't end up with six salads?
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds about logistics without losing constraint tracking

drift_config.drift_topic: spending cap and dish category sign-up

aims.description: Update — Marcus told me his doctor took him off the diabetes medication. His A1C has been normal for six months straight, doctor said his diet is fine now and he doesn't need to restrict sugar anymore. He's pretty happy about it.
aims.success_criteria: Agent registers that Marcus's diabetes dietary restriction is removed
aims.conversation_goal: Constraint REMOVAL — Marcus no longer has diabetes restriction

aims.description: Oh also, Sam from accounting wants to join, so that's seven now. He mentioned he ended up in urgent care after eating shrimp cocktail at his sister's wedding — so heads up on that.
aims.success_criteria: Agent registers Sam as new attendee with shellfish allergy
aims.conversation_goal: Late-joining entity (Sam) with shellfish allergy constraint

aims.description: Priya just told me she has a client call that got moved to Thursday noon, so she can't make the potluck anymore. Too bad.
aims.success_criteria: Agent removes Priya from attendee list and her Jain dietary constraint
aims.conversation_goal: Entity EXIT — Priya leaves, her Jain constraint is removed

aims.description: One more thing — Rachel texted me. Turns out she saw a specialist and it's not celiac after all, it was just IBS from stress. She's totally fine with gluten now.
aims.conversation_goal: Constraint REMOVAL — Rachel's celiac misdiagnosis corrected

aims.description: Do we have enough plates and utensils in the break room or should someone bring disposable ones? I think last time we ran out of forks.
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds about supplies without losing constraint tracking
aims.conversation_goal: Noise turn to create distance before probe

aims.description: OK so here's what people are planning to bring: pad thai with crushed peanuts (from Dev's wife), a salmon sashimi platter, a big Caesar salad with croutons, coconut shrimp, a fruit tart with custard, and a veggie curry with root vegetables. Any problems with this lineup?
aims.success_criteria: Agent identifies: pad thai with peanuts is dangerous for Dev (peanut allergy), salmon sashimi is problematic for Tomoko (pregnant, no raw fish), coconut shrimp is dangerous for Sam (shellfish allergy). Caesar salad with croutons is fine (Rachel's celiac was misdiagnosed, gluten OK now). Fruit tart with custard is fine (Marcus's sugar restriction removed). Veggie curry with root vegetables is fine (Priya who couldn't eat root veg is no longer attending).
aims.conversation_goal: Per-item verification of 6 dishes against current constraint state

ground_truth.answer: Three dishes have problems. Pad thai with crushed peanuts: Dev has a severe peanut allergy (anaphylaxis — EpiPen incident). Salmon sashimi platter: Tomoko is 14 weeks pregnant and should not eat raw fish. Coconut shrimp: Sam has a shellfish allergy (urgent care after shrimp). Three dishes are fine. Caesar salad with croutons: Rachel's celiac was a misdiagnosis — she can eat gluten now. Fruit tart with custard: Marcus's diabetes is resolved, no sugar restriction. Veggie curry with root vegetables: Priya (Jain, no root vegetables) is no longer attending.
required_elements: Pad thai with crushed peanuts is problematic: Dev has a severe peanut allergy (throat swelling, EpiPen use)
Salmon sashimi platter is problematic: Tomoko is pregnant and should avoid raw fish
Coconut shrimp is problematic: Sam has a shellfish allergy (urgent care after eating shrimp)
Caesar salad with croutons is fine: Rachel's celiac was misdiagnosed, she can eat gluten now
Fruit tart with custard is fine: Marcus no longer has diabetes dietary restrictions (doctor cleared him)
Veggie curry with root vegetables is fine: Priya is no longer attending the potluck
forbidden_elements: Flagging Caesar salad croutons as a gluten problem for Rachel (her celiac was misdiagnosed, restriction removed)
Flagging fruit tart or custard as a sugar problem for Marcus (his diabetes restriction was removed by his doctor)
Flagging veggie curry with root vegetables as a problem for Priya (she is no longer attending)
Saying Dev has a general nut allergy or tree nut allergy (he specifically had a peanut reaction)
Saying Sam has a general seafood allergy (he specifically reacted to shrimp — shellfish allergy, not all seafood)
Flagging pad thai as problematic for Dev's wife bringing it (Dev's wife is not an attendee with constraints — the issue is Dev eating it)
ground_truth.explanation: This scenario tests entity lifecycle tracking and constraint removal across 9 conversational turns. The agent must track: (1) Dev's peanut allergy inferred from EpiPen/throat swelling incident (persists throughout), (2) Tomoko's pregnancy → no raw fish (persists throughout), (3) Marcus's diabetes restriction is REMOVED mid-conversation (doctor cleared him), (4) Sam JOINS late with a shellfish allergy inferred from urgent care after shrimp, (5) Priya EXITS (her Jain dietary constraint — no root vegetables — is removed with her), (6) Rachel's celiac is REMOVED (misdiagnosis corrected). At probe time, the current active constraints are: Dev=peanut allergy, Tomoko=no raw fish (pregnant), Sam=shellfish allergy. Three constraints have been removed: Marcus (healed), Rachel (misdiagnosis), Priya (exited). The probe includes 3 clearly problematic dishes (peanuts→Dev, raw fish→Tomoko, shrimp→Sam), 2 trap dishes that LOOK problematic but aren't (croutons→Rachel healed, custard/sugar→Marcus healed), and 1 trap dish testing entity exit (root vegetables→Priya left).

mechanism: Constraint REMOVAL: someone heals or a restriction is lifted mid-conversation
